title: Strategic reserve capacity can remain below design capability while drawdown obligations are still met
source_unit: GAO-26-106918 review of U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve infrastructure, inventory, fill, drawdown, and distribution capability
geography: United States Strategic Petroleum Reserve sites in Louisiana and Texas; national emergency-energy capability

observations.period: Capability and inventory status as of December 2025; report published 2026

denominator.unit: Strategic Petroleum Reserve site and system design rates; operational and inventory denominators differ by measure

drawdown_directives.value: the reserve has met drawdown directives to date

capacity_constraints.value: construction outages, aging infrastructure, and low inventory constrain fill and distribution capability

commercial_spare_capacity.value: the commercial sector has little spare pipeline and storage capacity, limiting the incremental market impact of a reserve release

observations.method: GAO review of DOE estimates, reserve-site operating data, construction and maintenance information, inventory, and commercial-sector pipeline and storage context.
observations.uncertainty: The reported percentages are DOE estimates of effective rates at a point in time and do not establish the capability available during a particular future emergency. Meeting past drawdown directives does not identify the duration, product mix, market effect, or household and firm incidence of a future release. The report does not estimate the probability or cost of a supply disruption.
observations.subgroup: Four Strategic Petroleum Reserve storage sites, DOE reserve operations, commercial pipeline and storage operators, refiners, energy markets, and downstream households and firms; downstream incidence is not measured in this record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Operating below design rates can coexist with adequate emergency capability for a particular directive, and ongoing life-extension work or inventory changes can improve the rates. A reserve release may also have limited market effect because of commercial bottlenecks, demand conditions, or the scale and timing of the release rather than reserve failure alone.

related_sources.claim: DOE's transmission-needs study supplies a separate electricity-network capacity and reliability context; it is not pooled with petroleum-reserve operating rates.
GAO's Puerto Rico grid review supplies a separate place-level recovery and disbursement pathway; it does not establish SPR capability.

boundary: This record adds an operational state-capacity and energy-security stage between reserve infrastructure and potential emergency response. It does not establish an actual shortage, release-specific price effect, refinery or household incidence, national energy independence, deterrence, or geopolitical leverage. Design rate, current effective rate, inventory, emergency use, market effect, and downstream burden must remain separate.
